incidents.cause: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during a climbing turn after takeoff and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin at an altitude too low for recovery. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to operate the airplane
The failure of the pilot to maintain directional control of the airplane during final approach.
The failure of the torsional drive coupling, which resulted in a loss of drive to the main rotor system during low-altitude flight.
A partial loss of engine power due to a failure of the throttle interconnect hardware, which resulted in a hard landing.
A loss of directional control during the landing roll.
The pilot did not maintain directional control of the airplane while landing in gusty wind conditions.
